answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table due to the compliance-mandated security patch, eliminating memory_b1 as a candidate despite its historical success. The write-path latency climb during peak settlement traffic pattern-matches memory_b3 (headroom absorbing a surge) more closely than memory_b2's failover scenario, since failover risks splitting or losing in-flight writes during a payments peak — directly threatening the 'no lost customer writes' objective. Circuit breakers (b4) and read-replica routing (b5) don't address write-path capacity pressure; b4 assumes a dependency failure not yet confirmed, and b5 offloads reads, not the write bottleneck. I verified b3 and b2 to confirm the provisioning precedent actually involved a comparable surge (not a different bottleneck type) and to rule out that failover was cleanly reversible-with-writes before dismissing it. Given only one intervention is possible and root cause (load vs. release regression) isn't fully disambiguated, I'm scoping this as a guarded capacity add rather than a broad rollout, preserving the option to reassess next window rather than assuming this fully resolves the latency climb.
